name: Salesman Hal – AI Agent Ready: MCP, AI Visits & AI Booking
author: Salesman Hal

sections.description:
More customers ask an AI assistant before they call anyone: “find me a plumber who can come today.” The assistant reads a few sites, picks one, and more and more often tries to make the booking itself. Salesman Hal gets your business ready for those assistants, and shows you when they visit.

See which AI assistants visit your site

  • AI agent visits in wp-admin. See which AI agents (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and others) read your site and why: answering someone’s question, indexing for AI search, or collecting training data. “AI agents visited 14 times this week” right on your dashboard.
  • Ordinary visitors are never logged. Only requests from known AI agents are recorded, by user agent.

Let AI assistants work with your business

Connect your site and Hal gives it its own MCP server (the Model Context Protocol, the standard way AI assistants use outside tools). Assistants can then:

  • Answer questions accurately from your own pages, services, hours and contact details.
  • Send inquiries and quote requests into the forms you already use. Gravity Forms, Contact Form 7 and WPForms are supported. Requests arrive as normal form entries, so your usual notifications and CRM hooks fire. Consent checkboxes are never ticked for anyone. A form’s CAPTCHA (reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Turnstile) only works in a visitor’s browser, so these signed requests skip it; the service’s signature stands in for it.
  • Book meetings on your Calendly, once you connect it in your Salesman Hal dashboard.

An assistant has to confirm the visitor agreed before Hal sends anything, and every request is rate-limited.

Be found by AI agents

When your MCP server is on, the plugin publishes the files AI agents look for: /.well-known/mcp, /.well-known/mcp.json, the MCP server card, and a <link rel="mcp"> tag. It doesn’t touch your theme or your pages.

It also offers your MCP tools to AI agents that work inside the visitor’s browser, through WebMCP (in Chrome’s origin trial). This is always on.

If you choose to, it can also show a small “MCP for AI assistants, powered by Salesman Hal” line in your footer. AI assistants read your pages’ text, so a visible link helps them find your MCP server. It’s off unless you turn it on.

Free AI-readiness scan

Not sure where you stand? The free scan grades how well AI assistants can find, understand and act on any site, with a plain-language fix for every gap.

External service

This plugin works with the Salesman Hal service. Nothing is sent until you click Connect in Settings → Salesman Hal. After that it sends:

  • When you connect: your site’s address and name.
  • When content syncs (on save, daily, and on “Sync now”): the business details you enter in the settings; the title, text, address and publish date of published content of the types you choose (never password-protected pages, or pages marked noindex in Yoast or Rank Math); the fields of your lead forms (never their past submissions); and scheduling links found on your pages.
  • As AI visits happen (right after the page is delivered, where your host supports it), hourly as a retry, and on “Sync now”: for requests from known AI agents only, the agent’s user agent, the page path and the time.
  • The tracking pixel (on by default, after your site is verified): each page includes a 1×1 image loaded from the service, so every visitor’s browser or agent sends the service the page path (never its query string) along with the usual request details, such as IP address and user agent. The service stores a record only when the user agent is a known AI agent; requests from people aren’t stored, though its hosting provider may keep standard server logs for a short time. Turn the pixel off in the settings to stop this.
  • When you click “Open dashboard”: a request for a one-time sign-in link.

Your pages load a small script, webmcp.js, from the Salesman Hal service’s CDN. Like any file a page loads, fetching it sends the service the visitor’s IP address and browser type; Salesman Hal doesn’t store them, though its hosting provider may keep standard server logs for a short time. The script reads nothing on the page except the <link rel="mcp"> address. It does nothing unless the browser supports WebMCP. In a browser that does, it fetches your tool list from your MCP server, and an AI agent’s tool calls go there.

The service also:

  • fetches a verification code from your site once, to confirm you own the domain: /.well-known/salesman-hal-verification.txt, or, if your host doesn’t let WordPress answer /.well-known/, the plugin’s REST route /?rest_route=/salesman-hal/v1/verification;
  • sends inquiries and quote requests from AI assistants to your site’s salesman-hal/v1/submit REST endpoint, signed so only the service can use it. These contain what the visitor agreed to share, such as a name, email address, phone number and message, and become entries in your form plugin. The service keeps a copy for your Salesman Hal dashboard.
  • books meetings directly on your Calendly (when you’ve connected it in the dashboard) and records them in your Salesman Hal dashboard. Bookings don’t pass through your site or your form plugin.

Apart from the pixel and WebMCP script requests above, which Salesman Hal doesn’t store, nothing about ordinary human visitors is collected or stored. See the service’s terms of service and privacy policy.

Developers

  • salesman_hal_should_sync – skip a post.
  • salesman_hal_document / salesman_hal_document_type – adjust a synced post.
  • salesman_hal_forms – add or remove detected forms.
  • salesman_hal_lead_replayed – runs after a lead from an AI assistant is submitted to a form.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Settings → Salesman Hal, fill in your business details (including the business email, where requests are emailed if your site can’t take them), click “Save Changes”, then click “Connect to Salesman Hal”.
  3. If verification fails, make sure your site is public and your host or security plugin doesn’t block the WordPress REST API, then click “Verify again”.
  4. Click “Open dashboard” to see AI activity and connect Calendly.
sections.faq:
Does this slow my site down?

Barely. Checking a visitor’s user agent is a string match, and AI visits are sent to the service after the page has already been delivered (on hosts that support it), with an hourly background batch as the fallback, so visitors never wait. Pages also load one small script (webmcp.js, a few kilobytes) from the service’s CDN. It’s deferred, so it doesn’t hold up the page, and it does nothing unless the browser supports WebMCP.

Do I need to change my forms or theme?

No. Inquiries go into the forms you already have. If your form needs an answer the assistant didn’t give, Hal asks the assistant to get it from the visitor. If your site can’t take the request, it’s emailed to the business email in the plugin’s settings instead, so make sure that’s filled in.

My host caches pages. Will visits still be counted?

Cached pages never reach WordPress, so the plugin can’t see those requests directly. The optional tracking pixel (on by default) catches agents that load images. Once your site is verified, the pixel loads from the Salesman Hal service so those visits are counted immediately; only the page path is sent with it, never query strings.

Which pages do AI assistants see?

Published content of the post types you choose in the settings. Password-protected pages and pages marked noindex in Yoast or Rank Math are never synced.

Does the plugin update itself?

Only if you choose to. Tick “Keep Salesman Hal updated automatically” in Settings → Salesman Hal, or click “Enable auto-updates” for it on the Plugins screen (they’re the same setting). WordPress then installs new versions from WordPress.org in the background. Otherwise you update it like any other plugin.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating stops syncing and removes the discovery files. Deleting also removes the plugin’s settings and its visit log. Disconnecting stops all syncing and visit reporting, but what was already sent (your synced content, AI visit records, and leads and bookings) stays on the Salesman Hal service. To have it deleted, follow the instructions in the service’s privacy policy.

0.1.0

  • First release: connection and domain verification; content, form and booking-link sync; AI agent visit logging and dashboard widget; lead replay into Gravity Forms, Contact Form 7 and WPForms; MCP discovery files.
